title: What If All the Planets Lined Up in a Row?

scenes.text: What if every planet in the solar system lined up? Doomsday headlines say disaster. The math says otherwise.
The Moon has a tidal pull of about two. The Sun's pull is one. Venus, the strongest planet, is 0.0001.
Jupiter is more than two and a half times Earth's gravity, but its tidal tug on us is even smaller: 0.00001.
NASA estimates that if every planet lined up, ocean tides would rise by one twenty-fifth of a millimeter.
That is thinner than a human hair, and the planets are still tens of millions of miles apart.
So the great alignment would change nothing. The Moon moves your tides far more, twice every single day.

description:
What if all the planets lined up?
NASA estimates their combined gravity would raise ocean tides by only one twenty-fifth of a millimeter.
